issues.legal_issue: A tenant who attorns to a person claiming paramount title after a threat of eviction is not estopped from disputing the former landlord’s title in eviction proceedings brought by that former landlord.
material_facts: The tenant occupied the premises under a subtenancy created by the respondent.
The owner and head lessor served a notice threatening eviction because of unlawful subletting and stated that the respondent’s tenancy would be terminated.
Following the notice, the tenant attorned to the head lessor and agreed to pay rent directly to him.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was not estopped from disputing the respondent’s title or right to bring eviction proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 116 of the Evidence Act, 1872, a tenant generally cannot deny the landlord’s title at the commencement of the tenancy while continuing in possession received under that tenancy. The estoppel is limited in extent and time, and does not prevent a tenant from showing that the landlord’s title has ended or that the tenant attorned to a paramount title-holder under threat of eviction. A threat followed by attornment can constitute eviction by title paramount without actual dispossession or an ejectment suit; voluntary surrender does not qualify. The Court relied on Bilas Kunwar v. Desraj Ranjit Singh, Atyam Veerraju v. Pechetti Venkanna, Kumar Krishna Prosad Lal Singha Deo v. Baraboni Coal Concern, Adyanath Ghatak v. Krishna Prasad Singh, Mangat Ram v. Sardar Meharban Singh, Fida Hussain v. Fazal Hussain, K.S.M. Guruswamy Nadar v. N.G. Ranganathan, S.A.A. Annamalai Chettiar v. Molaiyan, Chidambara Vinayagar Devasthanam v. Duraiswamy, and Halsbury’s Laws of England, paragraph 238.

predicates.eviction_proceeding_by_former_landlord: A person who claims to be the landlord brings an eviction proceeding against a tenant who disputes that person’s title.
predicates.paramount_title_holder_threatened_evicti: A person with paramount title threatened to evict the tenant.
predicates.tenant_attorned_to_paramount_title_holde: The tenant, in response to the threat, recognized the paramount title-holder as landlord and agreed to pay rent to that person.
predicates.tenant_not_estopped_from_disputing_forme: The tenant is not barred from disputing the former landlord’s title.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding is brought by a former landlord after a paramount title-holder threatened eviction and the tenant attorned to that title-holder, the tenant is not estopped from disputing the former landlord’s title.

issues.legal_issue: Eviction for denial of the landlord’s title requires a finding that the denial was not bona fide.
material_facts: The respondent sought eviction on the ground that the tenant had denied his title.
The tenant disputed the respondent’s title after the head lessor threatened eviction and the tenant attorned to him.
The High Court made no finding that the tenant’s dispute as to title was not bona fide.
issues.conclusion: The eviction order could not be sustained on the ground of denial of title because there was no finding that the denial was not bona fide.
issues.legal_principle: Section 10(2)(vi) of the Andhra Pradesh Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1960 permits eviction for denial of the landlord’s title only where the denial or claim of a permanent tenancy is not bona fide. The Court held that the required finding was absent; in the circumstances, the tenant’s dispute following the threat of eviction by the title-holder could not be treated as a denial that was not bona fide.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: A landlord seeks eviction of a tenant under a statutory rent-control process.
predicates.tenant_denied_claimant_title: The tenant disputed the title of the person seeking eviction.
predicates.no_finding_denial_not_bona_fide: The decision-maker made no finding that the tenant’s denial of title was not bona fide.
predicates.eviction_not_authorized_on_title_denial: Eviction is not authorized on the ground that the tenant denied the claimant’s title.

issues.definition: In a rent-control eviction proceeding, if the tenant disputed the claimant’s title and there is no finding that the denial was not bona fide, eviction is not authorized on that ground.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant is not in default to a former landlord for rent paid to a paramount title-holder after the tenant attorns to that title-holder.
material_facts: After the head lessor threatened eviction, the tenant attorned to him and agreed to pay him rent directly.
The tenant paid rent to the head lessor after attornment and was not in arrears to him.
The respondent nevertheless sought eviction for non-payment of rent.
issues.conclusion: The tenant could not be treated as in arrears to the respondent after attorning to and paying rent to the head lessor, so eviction for default was unsustainable.
issues.legal_principle: Section 10(2)(i) of the Andhra Pradesh Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1960 concerns failure to pay or tender rent due to the landlord. After the tenant attorned to the head lessor, a direct tenancy arose between them; because the tenant paid rent to that lessor, the tenant could not be treated as in arrears to the former landlord.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: A landlord seeks eviction of a tenant under a statutory rent-control process.
predicates.tenant_attorned_to_paramount_title_holde: The tenant recognized the paramount title-holder as landlord and agreed to pay rent to that person.
predicates.tenant_paid_rent_to_paramount_title_hold: The tenant paid rent to the paramount title-holder after attorning to that person.
predicates.no_rent_default_to_former_landlord: The tenant is not in rent default to the former landlord for the period covered by those payments.

issues.definition: If a tenant in a rent-control eviction proceeding attorns to a paramount title-holder and pays rent to that person, the tenant is not in rent default to the former landlord for that period.
